teams.heading: Jake White outlines Fiji's 2027 World Cup plan, starting with Japan
teams.body: New Fiji coach Jake White used his Suva unveiling on Tuesday to outline a plan built on depth. White, the 2007 World Cup-winning Springbok coach, first faces Japan later this month, then France, Ireland and Italy in November. His immediate task is establishing who is eligible, available and injury-free. He also plans to watch club rugby and work with U18 and U20 coaches on a pathway for young players. "Next year is about building depth," he said, with the final block reserved for peaking before the World Cup.

lead.why: Jake White's unveiling plan is the freshest Fiji-specific detail in the pack, covering his priorities before Japan and the November Tests.

teams.heading: England's Ellis Genge and Courtney Lawes urge Premiership to publish salaries
teams.body: England prop Ellis Genge and lock Courtney Lawes have suggested making the wages of all English clubs public, arguing that rugby's secrecy over money is hurting the game commercially. Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Rugby podcast, Lawes said players are paid peanuts compared with footballers, cricketers and US sport, but that pay cannot outrun what the game earns. Genge said talk of transfer fees is open, unlike talk of pay, and he was surprised his own Leicester contract length was never published.

lead.why: It is a new story about England's own players, it is men's rugby, and it is the freshest item with a clear angle for an England fan.

teams.heading: France lock Thibaud Flament reportedly ruled out of November Tests
teams.body: Lock Thibaud Flament is reportedly out of France's November Tests with a shoulder injury, according to L'Équipe, leaving France coach Fabien Galthié short of another key option in the second row. The 29-year-old Toulouse forward, who played 80 minutes in Sunday's 45-34 Top 14 win over Bayonne, is said to face several weeks out. He had been tipped to pair with Emmanuel Meafou, himself recovering from a knee injury, for the Tests against Fiji, South Africa and Argentina.

lead.why: A new report of a France lock ruled out of the November Tests is the freshest France-specific story in the pack, and it bears directly on the Springboks and Fiji matches.

teams.heading: Ireland women's Aoife Dalton stars in 43-19 win over Japan in Cork
teams.body: Ireland women beat Japan 43-19 in Cork on Saturday 3 October, their second win over the Sakura XV in a week after the Galway result. Ireland scored three tries to race into a 22-7 lead, and flyhalf Dannah O'Brien's kicking caused Japan's defence serious problems. Japan, who had also lost in Galway, head home winless in four straight matches.

teams.heading: Italy sit 11th of 12 after three defeats, conceding 131 points overall
teams.body: Italy have won none of their three matches so far in the log, losing all three while scoring 37 points and conceding 131, a points difference of -94. The most recent was a 10-57 defeat to Australia in round three, and Italy's best world ranking remains No. 8, reached in 2007 and again in 2024. Those are the numbers Italy carry into the next round of the campaign.

teams.heading: Scotland have scored 348 points and conceded 299 in last 11 games
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Scotland have scored 348 points, an average of 31.6 a game. Over the same run they have conceded 299, or 27.2 a game. That leaves a net margin of 49 points in their favour across the 11 games. The biggest win in that window was a 56-0 home victory over Tonga in November 2025, an International Friendlies fixture.

teams.heading: Ben Thomas set to miss start of Wales' Nations Championship
teams.body: Ben Thomas, the Cardiff centre who started at inside centre in July's 43-0 defeat to South Africa in Durban, is set to miss the start of Wales' Nations Championship with a calf injury. Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl said: "He'll be able to definitely form part of the Nations Championship, but might not recover for the first or second game." Steve Tandy names his autumn squad next week, and Eddie James, usually selected at outside centre, is an option inside.

lead.why: A fresh BBC report on a Wales centre injury that affects the Nations Championship opener, and it is the NEW item most likely to change Tandy's selection planning.

teams.heading: Argentina fans unfurl Falklands banner in August's 10-17 defeat to South Africa
teams.body: Television cameras picked out a crowd banner reading "The Falklands are Argentine" during Argentina's 10-17 defeat to South Africa in August, the Pumas' first game since the 24-31 loss to England. Daniel Schofield of Yahoo Sports wrote that the banner showed the bad blood still lingers. Schofield credited Argentina's ferocious defence but said they fizzled out after a promising start as the Springbok bench turned the tide.

lead.why: The Edwards and Ledesma appointments have already run, and this is the richest fresh-to-the-pack story about Argentina's own supporters and the England rivalry.

teams.heading: Justin Marshall rates Harry Wilson world's best No. 8 despite Auckland thrashing
teams.body: Former All Blacks scrum-half Justin Marshall has handed Wallabies captain Harry Wilson the top number eight tag, calling him "the best number eight in the world at the moment" on The Good, The Bad & Rugby podcast. Wilson's case rests on Eden Park: he made a match-high 27 tackles, scored a try and won a crucial turnover in the 50-19 defeat to the All Blacks. Kieran Read, a former All Blacks number eight, questioned Marshall's "effortless" description but agreed Wilson's effort was all there.

lead.why: A new item on Wallabies captain Harry Wilson, not previously reported, and it is about an Australian player rather than background or a rival's view.

teams.body: Japan are on a current run of three straight wins. In their last five games, they have won three and lost two. teams.heading: Victor Matfield says Frizell, Barrett returns boosted All Blacks' Bledisloe rout
teams.body: Victor Matfield, former Springboks lock, reckons the return of Shannon Frizell and Scott Barrett bolstered New Zealand in the 50-19 Eden Park win over Australia. Speaking on the Rugby Rivals podcast, he said having those players back "coming off the bench" would make a big difference. Matfield also argued Australian Super Rugby sides' struggles against New Zealand clubs have left the Wallabies with a mental block against the All Blacks.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist that is about the All Blacks, and it gives a fresh, New Zealand-side view of the Bledisloe Cup result.

teams.heading: Eben Etzebeth and five Springboks to join Sharks' European tour squad
teams.body: Eben Etzebeth, initially a lower-limb concern, is set to join the Sharks' three-week European tour, and Planet Rugby reports the club expect him to be fit sooner rather than later. He joins Ox Nché, Thomas du Toit, Andre Esterhuizen, Ethan Hooker and Edwill van der Merwe, all of whom missed the Challenge Cup opener in France. Fez Mbatha, Makazole Mapimpi and Vusi Moyo remain in South Africa with knocks.

lead.why: New item on Springbok availability at the Sharks, which a South Africa fan will want to know about.
